name: Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies
ingredients:
225g unsalted butter, cubed
150g caster sugar
150g light brown sugar
3 large egg yolks
1oz whole milk
270g plain flour
1 1/2 tsp baking powder
3/4 tsp bicarbonate soda
3 tbsp cornstarch
150g dark chocolate, chopped
150g milk chocolate, chopped
instructions:
## Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies

**Brown the butter:** Cube the butter, then melt it in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring frequently, until golden brown with a nutty aroma, about 5–7 minutes. Watch closely so it doesn't burn. Let it cool slightly before using.

**Cream and mix:** In a large bowl, cream the browned butter with the caster sugar and light brown sugar. Add the egg yolks and milk, mixing until well combined.

**Combine dry and wet:** In a separate bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, and cornstarch. Gradually add to the wet mixture, stirring until a smooth dough forms.

**Fold in chocolate:** Gently fold in the dark and milk chocolate. Chopped chocolate (rather than chips) melts more evenly through the cookies.

**Chill:** Wrap the dough or transfer to an airtight container and refrigerate for at least 24 hours, up to 48 hours, to develop flavor and help the cookies hold their shape.

**Bake:** Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a light-coloured baking sheet with parchment paper, leaving space between cookies (about 3 per 30cm sheet). Scoop the chilled dough into balls onto the sheet. Optionally press extra chopped chocolate on top for a bakery-style finish. Bake 10–12 minutes, until golden brown around the edges — the centre may look underdone but will set as it cools.

**Cool:** Let the cookies rest on the baking sheet at least 6 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.
notes: Chilling the dough is the key step — it firms the butter, lets flavor develop, and hydrates the flour for a smoother, chewier bake. Use light-coloured baking sheets so the bottoms don't overcook before the centres are done. Raw dough balls can be frozen and baked straight from frozen (just add a couple of minutes).
